topics.title: Ancient civilizations (Grade 9)
topics.concept: Concepts of history, human evolution, Mesopotamia and Egypt, India and China, Greece and Rome.

subtopics.title: Concepts of history and sources
subtopics.concept: History is the scientific study of the human past. No history can be written without a source. Primary sources (letters, treaties, tools, paintings, eyewitness accounts) come from the period itself; secondary sources are later interpretations. Pre-history = the period before writing. Calendars: Babylonian lunar calendar 12 × 30 days; Egyptian solar calendar 12 × 30 days + 5 extra days.

textbook_refs.section: 1.3 Sources of History – forms of sources

subtopics.title: Human evolution and the rise of civilization
subtopics.concept: Order of hominids: australopithecines (first hominids, Africa) → Homo erectus → Homo sapiens (Neanderthals) → Homo sapiens sapiens (Cro-Magnon). Neolithic Revolution = systematic agriculture and permanent villages.

subtopics.title: Mesopotamia, Egypt and the Phoenicians
subtopics.concept: Hammurabi of Babylon issued a code of 282 laws (equal retaliation; patriarchal society – women had fewer rights, husbands could divorce wives who bore no children, children obeyed fathers). Egyptians preserved bodies by mummification. Phoenicians founded Carthage; Rome and Carthage fought the Punic Wars (264–146 B.C.E.).

subtopics.title: India and China
subtopics.concept: Caste system: Brahmins (priests) → Kshatriyas (warriors) → Vaisyas (commoners) → Sudras → Untouchables. Hinduism: reincarnation; created a legacy of inequality. Buddhism: Four Noble Truths, meditation. Chinese philosophies: Confucianism (government open to men of wisdom and skill, not only noble birth), Taoism, Legalism (people evil by nature → strong ruler). Chinese inventions: magnetic compass, paper, printing, gunpowder.

subtopics.title: Greco-Roman civilization
subtopics.concept: Greek philosophers: Socrates, Plato (The Republic), Aristotle (three good governments: monarchy, aristocracy, constitutional government). Oligarchy = rule by the few. Rome preserved and transmitted Greek civilization.

subtopics.title: Nubia (Kush) and Meroe
subtopics.concept: Nubia/Kush became independent of Egypt c. 1000 B.C.E.; its kings ruled on the Egyptian model and conquered Egypt (c. 750 B.C.E.) until driven out by the Assyrians (c. 670 B.C.E.). The capital moved from Napata to Meroe (iron ore, timber, rainfall, trade). Meroe was destroyed c. 350 C.E. by the Aksumite king Ezana.

topics.title: Ancient and medieval Eritrea (Grade 9 Unit 6)
topics.unit: G9 Unit 6 – Ancient and Medieval Eritrea
topics.concept: Peoples of Eritrea, Aksum and its decline, medieval developments, Turkish rule, Tigrean expansion and Egyptian rivalry.

subtopics.title: Peoples and social organisation of Eritrea
subtopics.concept: Linguistic groups: Nilotic (Nara, Kunama), Cushitic (Hidareb, Bilen, Saho, Afar), Semitic (Tigrinya, Tigre, Rashaida). Nara and Kunama: egalitarian, common linguistic family, crop cultivation + animal husbandry, clan administration by a council of elders. Bilen: Bet Taqwe moved from Hamasien to the Keren area (16th–17th c.), where Bet Tarke had already settled.

subtopics.title: The Aksumite kingdom and its decline
subtopics.concept: Aksum depended on Red Sea maritime trade; Christianity introduced c. 330–340 C.E. Decline from the 7th century: Persian conquest of Yemen and Arabia; rise and expansion of Muslim Arabia in the Red Sea (Adulis conquered 710 C.E.) which ended its trade; Beja migration and expansion (8th c.).

textbook_refs.section: 6.2 Ancient Eritrean Civilization – decline of the Aksumite Kingdom

subtopics.title: Medieval Eritrea (7th–19th centuries)
subtopics.concept: Key developments: Beja expansion and peaceful spread of Islam; Agew immigration; Turkish (1557 Massawa/Hirghigo) and Portuguese attempts at conquest in the 16th century; population movements; Tigrean and Amhara feudal expansion (18th–19th c.) to collect tribute, reach the coast for arms and profit from Red Sea trade. Raesi Wubie tortured people with hot roasted peas poured into their ears. Egypt–Tigrai-Amhara rivalry in the 19th century.

topics.title: Medieval and early-modern world (Grade 10 Units 1–11)
topics.concept: Medieval Europe and Byzantium, Islam, the Americas, African kingdoms, Renaissance and Reformation, exploration and slave trade, scientific revolution.

subtopics.title: Rise and expansion of Islam
subtopics.concept: Islam is monotheistic and accepts earlier prophets. Mohammed was persecuted in Mecca and fled to Medina in 622 – the Hijrah. His successors were caliphs (Abu Bakr first). Rapid expansion: Byzantine and Persian empires weakened by war, their subjects dissatisfied, local people accepted Arab rule, a large army with brilliant generals, religious motivation, Arab migration.

subtopics.concept: Maya: 300–900 C.E., Yucatán, city-states, temples and calendar. Ghana (from c. 500 C.E.) → Mali (Sundiata, mid-13th c., Timbuktu) → Songhai. East Africa: Swahili (Bantu + Arabic). Central Africa: Luba, Lunda, Kongo. Bantu spread over sub-Saharan Africa over two millennia.

subtopics.title: Renaissance and Reformation
subtopics.concept: Renaissance: urban, recovery from the 14th-century disasters, emphasis on individual ability; Machiavelli, The Prince. Reformation causes: corruption in the Church, worldly Renaissance popes, sale of indulgences, church taxes to Rome; Luther's Ninety-five Theses (1517).

subtopics.title: European exploration and the slave trade
subtopics.concept: Portugal took the lead in exploration (Prince Henry); Diaz 1488, Columbus 1492, da Gama 1498. Slavery existed in Africa before the Europeans; Europeans first bought slaves from local African merchants; the trade grew with the discovery of the Americas; 12–15 million Africans taken; West Africa most affected.

subtopics.concept: Mogul India: founded by Babur (descendant of Timur Lenk and Genghis Khan); Akbar followed a policy of religious tolerance; Muslim Moguls ruled a largely Hindu population; Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in Agra (1653) in memory of Mumtaz Mahal – 20,000 workers, more than twenty years.

subtopics.title: The Enlightenment
subtopics.concept: Voltaire: criticism of Christianity and religious tolerance; Montesquieu: separation of powers; Rousseau: the social contract; Diderot: the 28-volume Encyclopedia; Adam Smith founded modern economics – laissez-faire (the state should not interfere in the economy).

subtopics.title: Europe 1550–1715: wars of religion and absolutism
subtopics.concept: Philip II of Spain planned to invade England (1588 Spanish Armada) to protect Spanish ships and New-World colonies from English raids, to depose the Protestant Elizabeth I and to restore Catholicism in England; the Armada was defeated by the English. Louis XIV and the Bourbon dynasty; the Thirty Years' War (1618–1648).

subtopics.title: China and Japan 1400–1800
subtopics.concept: Ming dynasty (1368–1644; capital moved from Nanjing to Beijing in 1421). The Manchus, farming and hunting people from Manchuria north-east of the Great Wall, conquered Beijing and founded the Qing dynasty (1644–1911), China's last imperial dynasty. Tokugawa Japan.

subtopics.title: Asia 400–1500: China, the Mongols, Japan and Korea
subtopics.concept: Tang and Song China; the Mongols, a pastoral people from the Gobi desert, built the largest land empire in history under Genghis Khan (capital Karakorum, in modern Mongolia) and ended the Abbasid caliphate of Baghdad (1258). Early Japan: Shinto ('the Way of the Gods') – belief in kami and in the divinity of the emperor.

topics.unit: G10 Unit 12 – Italian Colonization in Eritrea
topics.concept: Italian expansion, colonial policy phases, administration, resistance.

subtopics.title: Italian expansion, policies and administration
subtopics.concept: Expansion helped by the Great Famine 1888–92, harsh Italian measures, and people tired of Tigrean/Egyptian raids. First phase (1890–96): settler colony, land alienation. Aims: settle poor Italian farmers; raw materials and market; springboard for expansion into Ethiopia. Justice: Italian penal code for all; civil code where one party was Italian; Sharia/customary law for Eritrean civil cases. Nakura island prison.

subtopics.concept: Degiat Aberra (Abera) Hailu killed Captain Pettini at Walta Medhanit (c. 1891); Bahta Hagos's revolt – wounded and died at Halay, December 1894; Abubaker Ahmed (Saho) led Saho and Tigrigna fighters (1901); Mohammed Nurri (Saho) planned to enter Asmara and kill Governor Ferdinando Martini (1902).

subtopics.title: American and French revolutions
subtopics.concept: George Washington commanded the Continental Army and became the first US president. French Revolution sequence: Estates-General (May 1789) → National Assembly → Bastille (14 July 1789) → Terror ends 1794 → Directory 1795 → Napoleon emperor 1804. The Third Estate = peasants, workers and the bourgeoisie (merchants, lawyers, doctors…).

subtopics.title: Industrialization, socialism and unification
subtopics.concept: Marx: history is the history of class struggle; bourgeoisie vs proletariat; proletariat would win; the state would wither away. Italian unification: Mazzini, Cavour, Garibaldi, Victor Emmanuel II (Bismarck unified Germany). Einstein: theory of relativity (1905).

Totalitarian regimes – Mussolini's Fascist Italy, Stalin's USSR, Hitler's Nazi Germany, Franco's Spain – demand total obedience, use massive propaganda, have a single leader and party and brutal security agencies. Interwar culture: mass culture (radio and movies), mass leisure, Dada and Surrealism, Joyce's Ulysses.

subtopics.title: British period and political parties (1941–1952)
subtopics.concept: Keren fell 27 March 1941, Asmara 1 April 1941 – end of Italian rule. Mahber Fiqri Hager founded 5 May 1941 (president Gebremeskel Woldu, vice-president Abdulkadir Kebire, secretary Haregot Abbay). Pro-independence leaders: Ibrahim Sultan, Woldeab Woldemariam, Abdulkadir Kebire; Tedla Bairu led the Unionists. Four Great Powers: USA, Britain, France, USSR.

topics.concept: Cold War, Asia and the Middle East since 1945, decolonization and independent Africa.

subtopics.title: The Cold War
subtopics.concept: NATO April 1949 (no Austria); Warsaw Pact 1955 (Soviet-led military alliance; Yugoslavia and Austria were not members). Sputnik I (1957) was the first man-made satellite. Berlin Wall (1961) = symbol of division. Bay of Pigs (1961) failed. Soviets crushed the Prague Spring in Czechoslovakia (1968). Gorbachev: perestroika. Former Yugoslavia: Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Macedonia, Serbia, Montenegro. Non-Aligned Movement grew out of Bandung (1955).

subtopics.concept: Israel proclaimed 14 May 1948; Knesset = parliament. PLO 1964; Six-Day War 1967; Camp David Accords 1978. Intifada = Palestinian uprising. subtopics.concept: Algeria fought a bloody war against France (independent 1962); Guinea chose full independence in 1958 under Sékou Touré. Tanzania's Ujamaa villages (Nyerere). Steve Biko's Black Consciousness aimed to restore black self-respect. Cold War aid: Soviet support to Ethiopia (Derg), Angola (MPLA), Mozambique, Somalia (until 1977).

topics.concept: ELM, ELF, zonal commands, Adobha, EPLF, strategic offensive, independence.

subtopics.title: ELM, ELF and the zonal commands
subtopics.concept: ELM founded November 1958 in Port Sudan (Mahber Showate). ELF founded in Cairo (1960), chairman Idris Mohammed Adem. ELF attacked the ELM at Ela Tsaeda (1965). Zonal commands (1965) copied from the Algerian Revolution. Adobha Conference (August 1969): national congress within one year, preparatory committee, committee to investigate misdeeds.
